key_insight: IBMARL bootstraps cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning from demonstrations collected one agent at a time, then learns decentralized policies that can outperform imitation alone.
engineering_relevance: The framework reduces the need to control multiple agents simultaneously during demonstration collection and removes centralized critics at deployment.
method: Train imitation policies with Round-Robin Behavior Cloning, controlling one agent while others follow their current policies.
Use centralized critic ensembles to select among combinations of each agent’s imitation and RL action proposals.
Apply a soft Q-filtered imitation penalty only where critics prefer imitation actions; deploy RL policies alone.
evidence_signal: Across four cooperative benchmarks, IBMARL surpassed its imitation policies 2.6–4.2× faster than demonstration-based baselines on two tasks and uniquely surpassed them on the other two; with real human demonstrations, it improved over imitation more than twice as fast as the best baseline.
watch_item: Selecting among joint action proposals can become costly as team size grows, and action selection depends on centralized critic accuracy.
